topic.definition: Data infrastructure, analytics, AI, digital twins or software platforms.
Machines or systems that perform physical or operational tasks with automated, remote, or autonomous control.
Methods and systems for observing asset condition, identifying defects, inspecting infrastructure, and deciding or carrying out maintenance.
Physical transmission network and its components: cables, converters, substations or HVDC systems.
The technical operation and control of the electricity system, including the use of flexibility or storage to manage grid conditions.
Market rules, trading and procurement arrangements, balancing services or congestion arrangements.
Offshore energy generation and its integration into a wider energy system.
Protection of people and critical infrastructure against hazards, security threats, failures, and disruptive events.
Environmental effects and sustainable practices: ecology, emissions or material use.
Reducing energy required for a given service, optimizing use of energy or replacing other energy with electricity.
Attracting, training and retaining the technical and professional workforce needed to build, operate and maintain the energy system.

role.definition: TenneT takes responsibility for directing the project or coordinating the consortium, including its work, partners, and delivery.
TenneT joins as a formal, non-leading project partner and takes responsibility for part of the work. This records its formal position; a more specific role can describe its contribution.
TenneT specifies and commissions work, equipment, technology, or services that another organisation delivers.
TenneT helps shape and create a new solution with other partners, making substantive decisions during development.
TenneT designs, implements, or operates an electricity-market or system-service arrangement, such as a balancing or congestion-management mechanism.
TenneT helps define or agree technical, operational, or procedural rules intended for use across organisations or systems.
TenneT provides data, access to infrastructure, a simulation setting, or an operational environment that others use to develop or test the solution.
TenneT contributes analysis, specialist knowledge, evidence, or research expertise to inform the project’s work.
TenneT provides money or institutional backing without commissioning a specific deliverable or performing a principal project activity.
TenneT contributes its perspective to policy or regulatory discussions, represents a position, or communicates project findings to relevant audiences.

activity.definition: Generates new knowledge to understand or solve a defined practical problem.
Examines options, requirements, expected benefits, feasibility, and risks to decide whether and how a proposed solution should proceed.
Turns an agreed concept into specifications, architectures, detailed designs, or engineering plans.
Builds or substantially improves a physical product, component, device, or prototype.
Creates or substantially improves software, analytical models, algorithms, data pipelines, or digital platforms.
Operates a solution on a limited scale or in a representative setting to show how it works in practice.
Checks a solution against defined requirements, performance criteria, or certification standards and produces evidence of the result.
Builds or materially upgrades physical grid or supporting infrastructure intended for continuing use.
Installs, integrates, or introduces a developed technology into practical use.
Changes how an existing system is monitored, coordinated, controlled, or operated.

activity.value: Asset Inspection, Maintenance or Life Extension
activity.definition: Inspects assets, assesses their condition, maintains or repairs them, or extends their useful life.

activity.value: Policy, Strategy, Standards or Regulation Development
activity.definition: Creates or revises formal policies, strategies, standards, regulatory proposals, or governance frameworks.

activity.value: Market, Contract or Flexibility Arrangement Development
activity.definition: Develops or revises market designs, flexibility arrangements, or electricity-market, system-service or grid-access contract structures before they are put into operation.
Improves the methods or processes used to plan, site, approve, or permit projects and infrastructure.
Establishes or strengthens cooperation structures that are themselves part of the project’s work.
Designs or carries out supplier tenders, framework agreements, insurance or other commercial arrangements that secure delivery capacity, risk cover or lower costs.

outcome.definition: Reduces the risk of injury or harm to employees or contractors.
Improves protection against cyberattacks, sabotage, or unauthorised access to assets, information, and operations.
Keeps existing assets functioning, reduces failures or downtime, restores service faster, or extends their useful life.
Ensures TenneT has the people, procedures, tools, materials, and arrangements needed to operate and maintain systems safely and reliably.
Reduces harm to the climate or natural environment through lower emissions, material use, or reduced ecological disturbance.
Delivers a defined level of performance using less money, labour, energy or logistical effort.
Makes more electricity transmission capacity available or brings new or upgraded connections into service sooner.
Keeps the power system within its frequency, voltage and dynamic stability limits, so that disturbances are damped and do not escalate into wider outages.

outcome.value: System resilience and security of supply
outcome.definition: Reduces the risk that the electricity system cannot meet demand or stay within secure operating limits, including under extreme weather, uncertainty or cascading events.
Increases the volume or accessibility of flexibility, such as demand response, storage, vehicles or redispatch bids, that TenneT can use to balance the system or relieve congestion.
Enables equipment, control systems or data platforms from different suppliers or organisations to work together through common specifications and interfaces.
Makes electricity-market, allocation or grid-tariff arrangements more efficient, fair or cost-reflective, so that they give sound signals for dispatch, investment and grid use.
Ensures TenneT meets new or changing legal and regulatory obligations, such as data-provision, reporting, technology-use or system-operation requirements.
Increases the number of skilled people available to TenneT and its supply chain to build, operate and maintain the grid.
Gives market parties, authorities or the public timely and reliable information about the electricity system, so they can make informed choices.
